sk-a2272b62.stem: The vertebral artery usually begins its ascent by entering the foramen transversarium of which vertebra?
sk-a2272b62.explanation: The vertebral artery, the first branch of the subclavian artery, typically enters the foramen transversarium of C6, ascends through the foramina of C6–C1 and enters the skull through the foramen magnum. Usually only the vertebral vein passes through the foramen transversarium of C7.

sk-75fe34b4.stem: Which vertebra has the most prominent spinous process palpable at the back of the neck?
sk-75fe34b4.explanation: The long, non-bifid spinous process of C7 is easily felt at the base of the neck and is used as the starting point for counting vertebrae. The spinous processes of C2–C6 are short and bifid.

sk-2b8ee94c.stem: Which vertebrae have articular facets (costal facets) for the head of a rib on their bodies?
sk-2b8ee94c.explanation: Thoracic vertebrae carry facets for the head of the rib on their bodies and, on their transverse processes (except T11–T12), facets for the rib tubercle. Their bodies are heart-shaped and their spinous processes long and sloping downwards.

sk-98dc357c.stem: The mammillary and accessory processes are characteristic of which vertebrae?
sk-98dc357c.explanation: Lumbar vertebrae have a mammillary process on the posterior border of the superior articular process and an accessory process at the root of the transverse process; deep back muscles attach to them. Their bodies are large and kidney-shaped, with no foramen transversarium or costal facet.

sk-d9e58822.stem: Through which opening is the needle inserted for caudal epidural anaesthesia?
sk-d9e58822.explanation: Because the laminae of S4–S5 do not fuse, the sacral hiatus remains on the back of the sacrum. The sacral cornua on either side guide the way, and the needle is advanced into the epidural space within the sacral canal.

sk-0bec5b45.stem: Which structure forms the posterior boundary of the pelvic inlet?
sk-0bec5b45.explanation: The pelvic inlet is bounded behind by the promontory, at the sides by the arcuate line and pecten pubis, and in front by the upper border of the pubic symphysis. The obstetric conjugate is the shortest distance between the promontory and the back of the symphysis.

sk-db733329.stem: After heavy lifting, a 45-year-old man describes pain radiating from the low back to the outer leg, dorsum of the foot and big toe, with weakness of big toe dorsiflexion. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: S1–S2 disc herniation compressing the S2 root
L5–S1 disc herniation compressing the S1 root
L4–L5 disc herniation compressing the L5 root
L1–L2 disc herniation compressing the conus medullaris
L3–L4 disc herniation compressing the L4 root
sk-db733329.explanation: Lumbar disc herniations are usually posterolateral and compress the root below: an L4–L5 herniation affects the L5 root. L5: sensation of the outer leg, dorsum of the foot and big toe, and strength of extensor hallucis longus. S1: lateral border of the foot, ankle reflex; L4: knee reflex and inner leg.

sk-2249b2c3.stem: Which ligament holds the dens of the axis against the anterior arch of the atlas?
sk-2249b2c3.explanation: The transverse ligament of the atlas (the horizontal limb of the cruciform ligament) wraps around the back of the dens and presses it against the anterior arch of the atlas. Its rupture (e.g. rheumatoid arthritis, Down syndrome) can let the dens compress the spinal cord.

sk-e8c060fb.stem: The sternal angle, used as the reference for counting ribs in chest examination, is at the level of which costal cartilage?
sk-e8c060fb.explanation: The sternal angle (angle of Louis) is the junction of the manubrium and the body of the sternum, and the 2nd costal cartilages articulate on either side of it. It is easily felt on the front; the 2nd rib is found and counting proceeds downwards.

sk-5ac9e561.stem: Which of the following about the horizontal plane through the sternal angle (T4–T5) is FALSE?
options: The aortic arch begins and ends at this plane.
The oesophagus passes through the diaphragm at this level.
The azygos vein opens into the superior vena cava at this level.
It separates the superior and inferior mediastinum.
The trachea bifurcates at this level.
sk-5ac9e561.explanation: The sternal angle plane is an important landmark of the chest: the boundary of the superior/inferior mediastinum, the tracheal bifurcation, the beginning and end of the aortic arch, the opening of the azygos vein into the SVC and the crossing of the thoracic duct to the left all lie at this level. The oesophagus passes through the diaphragm at T10.

sk-b9caecf9.explanation: Ribs 1–7 are true ribs attached directly to the sternum. The cartilages of ribs 8–10 join the cartilage above (false ribs). The anterior ends of ribs 11–12 are free (floating ribs).

sk-be399078.stem: Which structure runs in the groove behind the scalene tubercle on the first rib?
sk-be399078.explanation: Scalenus anterior attaches to the tubercle of the 1st rib. The subclavian vein lies in the groove in front of the tubercle; the subclavian artery and the lower trunk of the brachial plexus lie in the groove behind it (groove for the subclavian artery). The artery and plexus pass through the scalene gap, the vein in front of the muscle.

sk-1ca5b2b4.stem: During thoracentesis, where should the needle be passed to protect the intercostal vessels and nerve?
options: Just above the upper border of the rib below
Just below the lower border of the rib above
Through the costal groove medial to the angle of the rib
sk-1ca5b2b4.explanation: The intercostal vein, artery and nerve (VAN from above down) run in the costal groove on the lower border of the rib. The needle is therefore passed over the upper border of the rib below.

sk-b337c3b1.stem: A young woman has numbness and coldness of the hand when she raises her arm; a neck X-ray shows a cervical rib. Which structure is most often compressed in this condition?
options: Upper trunk of the brachial plexus (C5–C6)
Lower trunk of the brachial plexus (C8–T1)
sk-b337c3b1.explanation: A cervical rib (from C7) causes thoracic outlet syndrome. The lower trunk (C8–T1) and subclavian artery are compressed as they cross the rib or its fibrous band; there are paraesthesiae along the ulnar border of the hand, weakness of the intrinsic muscles and vascular signs.
